instruction_overrides.nourriture-001: For this word, kh is a single voiceless velar fricative /x/, like the final sound in Scottish loch, never an ordinary k and never k followed by h. Keep the vowel short. Finish with b immediately followed by voiced z, without adding a vowel between them and without changing z to s. Read the single supplied Moroccan word only.
instruction_overrides.chiffres-017: For this word, start with ch /ʃ/ immediately followed by the deep voiceless pharyngeal fricative 7 /ħ/. The 7 is a consonant, never seven, sept, or an ordinary h. Finish the Moroccan question with al and a clear final l. Do not spell the characters or insert an extra word; read the supplied word once.
instruction_overrides.verbes-085: This is one Moroccan verb, meaning to sign. Start with consonant w and a very short unstressed vowel. The sequence 99 is one sustained geminate uvular stop /qː/, never ninety-nine, nine nine, or letters pronounced separately. After a short unstressed vowel, finish with the voiced pharyngeal consonant 3 /ʕ/, not a numeral and not a vowel replacing that consonant. Keep all these sounds within one word. Read only the supplied Latin word once; do not speak this guidance.
instruction_overrides.adjectifs-052: This Moroccan word means thirsty. Begin with the voiced pharyngeal consonant 3 /ʕ/, never the word three or trois. Preserve the following t and ch /ʃ/ in sequence, then a and a clear final n. Do not omit the first consonant or the t, do not spell the Latin characters, and do not substitute a French or English word. Read the supplied Moroccan word once.
